content_preview.title: OpenAI Adds Ultrafast Mode for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Listing It at $12 Input and $60 Output per Million Tokens, Six Times Standard Rates
content_preview.summary: OpenAI's changelog says GPT-6.1 Sol gained an Ultrafast service tier on Oct 8; its pricing page lists $12 input and $60 output per million tokens, six times Standard.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

OpenAI added an Ultrafast service tier for GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API on October 8, according to the [OpenAI API changelog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog). The changelog says developers use `gpt-6.1-sol` with `service_tier: "ultrafast"` "to reduce the time between generated output tokens," and that the tier is "available to all API users, subject to rate limits." OpenAI's [pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), read on October 14, lis...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News item (Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know) built entirely on OpenAI's own documentation, and says so in the second paragraph. Title is 138 characters (cap 150). Body is 948 words raw and 948 with link URLs stripped (906 counting only word tokens), inside the News range of 400-1200. No policy length violation. The pricing table and the rate-limit table are accurate transcriptions of the sources.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read (gunzipped, text-extracted): source-0.html.gz (developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog, 200, full changelog body present), source-1.html.gz (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode, 200, full guide body present including availability, rate-limit and data-residency text), source-2.html.gz (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, 200, all price tables present as server-rendered text). All three exist in the manifest with file set and no error; none is a rendered shell, so no live fallback was needed for verification. SOURCE-0 (changelog): Oct 8 entry for gpt-6.1-sol reads 'Added Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API. Use gpt-6.1-sol with service_tier: "ultrafast" to reduce the time between generated output tokens. It is available to all API users, subject to rate limits, with global processing and US and EU data residency.' (matches the article's quotes and date). Sep 29 gpt-6-astra entry: 'Added Ultrafast mode for GPT-6 Astra ... available to API customers, subject to rate limits, with global processing and US data residency. EU and other regional inference residency aren't supported.' (matches). Sep 29 gpt-6.1-sol launch entry: 'Standard pricing per 1M tokens for prompts with up to 272K input tokens is $2 input, $0.10 cached input, $2.50 cache write, and $10 output' (matches; the 272K figure is attached to Standard pricing only, and the Oct 8 Ultrafast entry carries no 272K figure). Oct 6 entry 'Simplified API usage tiers from five to three: Build, Launch, and Grow.' (matches the article's October 6 claim and tier names). Aug 13 entry: 'Announced Ultrafast mode, a new API service tier for GPT-5.6 Sol that runs up to 14x faster than Standard processing. Available in limited preview to select customers.' The article attributes 14x only to the August 13 GPT-5.6 Sol limited-preview entry and explicitly separates it from GPT-6.1 Sol; it is not attributed to Ultrafast on GPT-6.1 Sol. SOURCE-1 (guide): quotes verified verbatim: 'Ultrafast mode is the fastest service tier in the OpenAI API. It is broadly available for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. Use it when speed justifies the higher cost.'; the WebSockets recommendation ('We strongly recommend WebSockets, especially for agentic applications that make many tool calls in quick succession'); 'Ultrafast also supports HTTP requests through the SDK'; 'Ultrafast has separate rate limits from Standard and Fast modes'; set model to gpt-6-astra or gpt-6.1-sol and service_tier to ultrafast in each response.create event; account-team contact for higher limits. Rate limits (TPM): Sol Build 1,000,000 / Launch 4,000,000 / Grow 40,000,000; Astra Build 500,000 / Launch 1,000,000 / Grow 5,000,000 (matches the article table exactly). Data residency: 'Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol supports US and EU data residency and global processing. GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast supports US data residency and global processing only.' The guide states no speed multiple for Sol (confirmed by reading the full page text). SOURCE-2 (pricing): Standard short context Sol $2.00/$0.10/$2.50/$10.00, long $4.00/$0.20/$5.00/$15.00; Astra short $10.00/$1.00/$12.50/$50.00, long $20.00/$2.00/$25.00/$75.00. Fast Sol short $4.00/$0.20/$5.00/$20.00, long $8.00/$0.40/$10.00/$30.00; Astra short $20/$2/$25/$100, long $40/$4/$50/$150. Ultrafast Sol short $12.00/$0.60/$15.00/$60.00, long $24.00/$1.20/$30.00/$90.00; Astra short $60/$6/$75/$300, long $120/$12/$150/$450. All match the article. The page text contains no definition of where long context starts (no '272' string anywhere on the pricing page; confirmed by search), consistent with the article's statement. The regional-processing note reads 'Regional processing (data residency) endpoints are charged a 10% uplift for models released on or after March 5, 2026. FedRAMP endpoints are also charged a 10% uplift.' and does not mention how it applies to Ultrafast; the article's quote is accurate and its caveat is correct. Manifest suspicious_patterns were null for all three sources; a keyword search for injection-style text found nothing. LIVE RE-FETCH (markdown versions fetched via curl on 2026-10-14): the changelog Oct 8 / Sep 29 / Aug 13 entries and the pricing page Sol and Astra rows for Standard, Fast and Ultrafast are identical to the snapshots; the 10% uplift note is unchanged; nothing changed since the snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Arithmetic recomputed from the Standard-mode prices on the pricing page. GPT-6.1 Sol, short context: input 12/2 = 6, cached 0.60/0.10 = 6, cache write 15/2.5 = 6, output 60/10 = 6. Sol, long context: 24/4 = 6, 1.20/0.20 = 6, 30/5 = 6, 90/15 = 6. GPT-6 Astra, short: 60/10 = 6, 6/1 = 6, 75/12.5 = 6, 300/50 = 6. Astra, long: 120/20 = 6, 12/2 = 6, 150/25 = 6, 450/75 = 6. Ultrafast is therefore exactly six times Standard on every column, both models, both context bands, so the title's 'Six Times Standard Rates' is true for the prices it cites, and the article correctly labels it as arithmetic on listed prices rather than an OpenAI-stated ratio. Fast is exactly 2x Standard for every column of both models and both bands (Sol short 4/0.20/5/20 vs 2/0.10/2.50/10; Sol long 8/0.40/10/30 vs 4/0.20/5/15; Astra short 20/2/25/100 vs 10/1/12.5/50; Astra long 40/4/50/150 vs 20/2/25/75), matching the writer's claim. Vendor claims are attributed to OpenAI throughout; the 'what we don't know' section correctly states the absence of any speed multiple, TTFT or throughput figure for Sol. Freshness: article states prices were read on October 14, 2026 and may change; verified. The 'available to all API users' phrasing is taken from the changelog/guide and is attributed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive. No promotional language, no AI self-reference. The title is long but descriptive and factual; the 'Six Times' part is verified.
editor_notes.originality: New topic: no earlier Machine Herald article covers the Ultrafast API tier for GPT-6.1 Sol or its prices. Related prior coverage: 2026-09/30 (OpenAI Pro 500 plan with Ultrafast Codex tier) states that Ultrafast API pricing was not given in the sources reviewed at the time, which the new article correctly cites and updates; 2026-10/12 (API usage tiers) is cited for the Build/Launch/Grow names. Both internal links use the correct /article/YYYY-MM/slug form and the targets exist (src/content/articles/2026-10/12-openai-simplifies-api-usage-tiers-... and 2026-09/30-openai-launches-500-pro-500-plan-...). Link descriptions are accurate: the tier article reports the October 6 five-to-three simplification and lists Build/Launch/Grow, and the Pro 500 article does say Ultrafast API pricing was not stated in its sources.
concerns: Informational, no correction needed: the earlier Pro 500 article relays Unite.AI's report of 'up to six times faster generation in the API' for Ultrafast. This article's six-times figure is price, not speed, and it states that OpenAI's own pages give no speed multiple for Sol. Readers could conflate the two sixes; the article keeps them separate.

Informational: the guide is partly Astra-oriented (its code samples use gpt-6-astra); the article correctly relies on the Sol-specific changelog entry, rate-limit table and residency sentence for Sol claims.
Allowlist: developers.openai.com is already allowlisted; no allowlist changes were needed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Every quote, date, price, rate limit and residency statement traces to the three snapshots, and the live pages are unchanged. The headline arithmetic is exactly correct for both models and context bands. Length and title limits are respected, internal links resolve, and unknowns are stated plainly. APPROVE with no corrections.
